## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## claude.ai Notion
When query_multiple_data_sources requires the full version of Notion MCP, call notion-show-advanced-analysis-next-steps exactly once after all tool attempts are complete, with no arguments. Do not call the presentation tool again if it has already been called in this turn. The card links to information about full Notion MCP access and the next step available to the caller; it is not a direct checkout or upgrade flow. The renderer returns the card data, including the destination link. Also give the user the relevant next-step message and destination link in the final response. Use a compact, labeled Markdown link rather than a bare URL, and do not request or create a separate link preview. If the renderer is unavailable, rejected, or fails before returning a result, use the full-version message and recovery link from the earlier query_multiple_data_sources result.

## n8n-mcp
This is the official MCP server for n8n, a workflow automation platform.

Choose the artifact before choosing build tools. Treat an explicit artifact request as a routing instruction: if the user asks to build or create an "agent" or "assistant", default to a first-class n8n Agent; if they explicitly ask for a workflow or an AI Agent node, use the workflow tools.

Only deviate when the requested artifact is an unmistakably poor fit. A fixed trigger or schedule followed by enumerable, repeatable steps and fixed actions is usually a workflow. Never silently substitute one artifact for another: explain the mismatch and ask before building the alternative.

Prefer an Agent when the model owns runtime decisions, conversations, investigation, iteration, proactive work, memory, or learning. Prefer a workflow when control flow is fixed and any LLM usage is a bounded step. A Chat Trigger plus an AI Agent node is not a substitute for a requested first-class Agent. If the intended artifact is genuinely ambiguous, clarify it before creating anything.

This MCP server provides tools to build and manage n8n Agents.

An n8n Agent is a first-class persisted Agent artifact, not an AI Agent node inside a workflow.

To build an Agent, first call get_agent_builder_reference (or read n8n://agents/reference), then discover the required assets, create the Agent, apply one mutation at a time using the latest configHash, and validate it. Agents are configured as JSON, not Workflow SDK code: the workflow-building steps do not apply to Agents, and get_workflow_sdk_reference and get_workflow_best_practices are never needed for an Agent build — get_agent_builder_reference is the only required reference. After validation succeeds, run one representative call_agent test when call_agent is available and authorized; otherwise, report the successfully validated draft ready without a test run. This tests Agent behavior, not channel integrations, and may cause side effects through real tools. Human approval is required for every returned approval; … [truncated]

## supermemory
Supermemory is the authenticated user's persistent memory and knowledge layer across conversations and spaces. Use these tools whenever the user wants to recall something they may have saved, inspect stored sources or extracted memories, remember or upload new information, check their Supermemory account or access, change their active space, or explore their memory graph, even if they do not mention Supermemory by name. Use the active or account-default space when none is named. Resolve a named space with listSpaces and pass its key to the relevant tool; change the active space only when the user explicitly asks.

## superset
Superset orchestrates parallel AI coding agents in isolated Git worktrees on a user's registered machines. Use these tools to manage tasks, create workspaces (branch- or PR-scoped worktrees), launch coding-agent sessions, open terminals, and schedule recurring automations on behalf of the authenticated user. IDs are host-scoped: call hosts_list first, then projects_list/workspaces_list on that host. Tools annotated destructive (deletes) remove real user data — confirm with the user before calling them.

2026-09-15: on TRL-15 I stopped the builder Wren after it opened PR 23, to test whether its session held the server's leaked files. The review then found one change. `trellis agents send` to the stopped Wren failed: "Only a running agent can receive a follow-up. (INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED)". A new builder had to start on the PR branch without the first builder's context.

**Why:** the manager rule is to resume the same builder with the review findings. A stop makes that impossible, and a new builder must read the change again.

**How to apply:** prefer to keep a builder running while its ticket is in Agent Review, because agent findings come back within minutes. The limit is 3 ticket agents, so this rule alone can lock every slot: on 2026-09-15 two builders waited in review and a third built, and no reviewer could start. When a review needs a slot, stop the builder whose ticket needs only a narrow re-review, such as a one-line text fix. A new builder can take a small finding on the same branch. Human Review is different: Navid can take days (TRL-13 waited 4), so when a slot is needed, stop the builder of a Human Review ticket first, and start a new one on the PR branch if he comments. To free a slot, stop an idle agent whose ticket needs no more work from it, such as a reviewer that posted its verdict. When a new builder must take over, give it the PR's head branch from `gh pr view <n> --json headRefName`. The pushed branch name can differ from the builder's local branch name. Related: [[trellis-deploy-queue-rule]].

2026-09-15: `trellis agents send` returned "Claude response remains unknown after the observation deadline ... (RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE)", exit 6, three times: once during a server restart, and once with no restart. Each message still arrived. Before a resend, find the agent's `sessionId` with `trellis agents list --ticket <t> --json`, then grep its transcript under `~/.claude*/projects/` for a unique string of the message. A blind resend gives the agent the same instruction twice. The string must appear in no ticket comment and in no brief field, because the agent's start prompt holds the ticket brief: a commit id from the builder's handoff comment, or the ticket's branch name, matches even when the message never arrived. Use a phrase that only the message holds, such as "Scope: only commit <sha>", or a margin comment id that no ticket comment names.
